item.title: FMC rejects requests by carriers to waive waiting period for Middle East surcharges | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The decision means CMA CGM, Hapag-Lloyd, Maersk and Zim will be forced to wait until early April before implementing surcharges designed to recoup higher operating costs associated with the war in the Middle East.

item.title: ONE takes stake in Busan’s Dongwon terminal ahead of Premier network shift | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The carrier alliance will shake up its Asia-Europe network in April with Busan becoming the focus of its North Asia trade and direct calls ending to ports in Japan and Taiwan.

item.title: US Gulf breakbulk ports lean into project boom | Journal of Commerce
item.description: Houston and New Orleans are coming off a year of growth for project cargo volumes, albeit with a drop in steel imports, and both ports anticipate a continuation of those trends.

item.title: UP adjusts intermodal pricing to win back volume as truckload rates climb | Journal of Commerce
item.description: Union Pacific for the second time in five weeks is resetting freight-all-kinds rates on key lanes for rail-owned boxes used by intermodal marketing companies.

item.title: War hands railroads the ‘gift’ of higher diesel prices | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The Iran-driven fuel spike has created the widest intermodal cost advantage in years, but capturing it — and keeping it — requires something railroads have rarely practiced: orchestrated intermodal, writes Paul Tonsager.

item.title: Singapore bunker supply continues to run down as Middle East war drags on | Journal of Commerce
item.description: With more than 50% of the city-state's bunker fuel imported via the Strait of Hormuz, which has been effectively closed since the war started on Feb. 28, suppliers are feeling the pinch.

item.title: Jump in diesel prices alone not enough to boost intermodal fortunes – analyst | Journal of Commerce
item.description: While the price of fuel has historically served as a tailwind for modal conversion, in and of itself, it is insufficient to guarantee success, writes Ted Prince.

item.title: Veteran PRPA, Fairview terminal executive to lead Prince Rupert port | Journal of Commerce
item.description: Kurt Slocombe will guide the Western Canadian port in completing a transload and logistics facility while attempting to create a boom in commodity exports and recover volume share lost during the COVID-19 pandemic.

item.title: Rubio, in escalation, criticizes China for detaining Panama-flag ships | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The comments by the US Secretary of State heighten the Trump administration’s involvement a week after the top federal maritime regulator flagged the ship detentions.

item.title: SeaLead warns of network disruptions in Persian Gulf war zone | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The announcement comes as the Singapore-based regional carrier outlined a strategic restructuring of its overall operations, including scaling down trade coverage across its key intra-Asia trade territories.

item.title: Rising jet fuel costs challenging freighter viability as war enters second month | Journal of Commerce
item.description: Global jet fuel prices have almost doubled since the Middle East war began on Feb. 28, piling additional expenses onto an operating component that before the conflict was already more than 30% of total costs.

item.title: CMA CGM said to have deal with Iran to allow safe passage through Hormuz: sources | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The CMA CGM Kribi successfully transited the strait late Thursday, the first passage for a Western-operated container ship since the war between the US/Israel and Iran disrupted access to the crucial waterway five weeks ago.

item.title: FMC again rejects Maersk petition to waive notice period for emergency fuel surcharge | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The unanimous decision prevents the carrier from immediately implementing the fee, which is meant to help recoup fuel costs on US trades that have been driven higher due to the war with Iran.

item.title: Charleston looking for retailer shippers to revive port’s growth | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The port’s chief executive said his agency will do more to attract large retail BCOs to reverse lost market share, while also investing in non-container projects.

item.title: Montreal Port chief Gascon exits abruptly after two-year tenure | Journal of Commerce
item.description: The departure of the Montreal Port Authority CEO comes just as development work begins on a new US$1.15 billion container terminal.
